key_insight: VLM-IE3D makes vision-language models more 3D-aware by combining two forms of geometric understanding: implicit geometric priors and explicit geometric representations learned from RGB videos. This helps the model reason better about spatial structure in 3D tasks.
problem_solved: Most VLMs are trained on 2D images and struggle with tasks that require accurate 3D spatial understanding, such as depth, layout, object relations, and viewpoint-aware reasoning.
method: Introduces Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs) to encode high-level 3D geometric priors in a compact latent form.
Learns Explicit Geometry Tokens (EGTs) to represent more direct, structured 3D geometric information from RGB video.
Combines both implicit and explicit geometries in a unified VLM framework to improve 3D reasoning across downstream tasks.
impact: This approach can help practitioners build VLMs that generalize better to real-world spatial tasks, especially in robotics, AR/VR, autonomous systems, and embodied AI. It offers a practical path for improving 3D reasoning without relying solely on expensive 3D sensors.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing RGB video input flowing into implicit and explicit geometry branches.

paper_title: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
paper_authors: Wenhao Li, Xueying Jiang, Quanhao Qian, Deli Zhao, Ran Xu
